title: fix: allow 127.0.0.1 redirects for local website auth
author: afanasevmylife
pr_body_excerpt:
- Documents the website key’s registered `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` redirect addresses and existing any-port behavior.
- Keeps exact hostname matching unchanged; the live registration fix was applied separately.
- Removes the broader OAuth matcher change and its associated test. Final diff: two comment lines in one file.

Fixes #14361

gist.headline: Loopback, properly labeled
gist.blurb: The website auth map now labels its two local garden gates: localhost and 127.0.0.1. Same paths, fewer future archaeology expeditions.
gist.summary: Documented that website keys register both localhost and 127.0.0.1 redirect addresses with existing any-port support, while exact hostname matching remains unchanged.
gist.impact: Developers can now see the intended local OAuth redirect behavior directly in the website API configuration without changing production matching rules.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy local-development garden shed with two clearly labeled loopback gates, one reading “localhost” and one reading “127.0.0.1,” both leading toward a small retro login terminal. Polli, wearing tiny developer glasses and holding a clipboard, checks the labels while code-vines and pixel flowers grow around the shed.
